Where is the Red Temple on Koh Samui? | On the seaward side of the ring road (Route 4169) about 2 km south of central Lamai, between Hin Ta and Hin Yai and Hua Thanon; GPS 9.4512, 100.0309.
What is the Red Temple's real name? | Its official name is Wat Ratchathammaram; locals call it Wat Sila Ngu after its chedi, Phra That Sila Ngu, and visitors call it the Red Temple.
Is the Red Temple on Koh Samui free? | Yes, entry is free; there are donation boxes if you want to support the temple.
What are the Red Temple's opening hours? | It is open daily 07:00–17:00; hours can change on public holidays.
What should I wear to the Red Temple? | Cover shoulders and knees before entering any building, and take your shoes off inside the hall.
What does Sila Ngu mean? | In Thai, sila means stone or rock and ngu means snake, so the name translates roughly as snake rock; we have not found a reliable account of its origin.
How long do I need at the Red Temple? | About 30 minutes is enough to walk around the carved hall, see the chedi and the sea view.
When is the best time to photograph the Red Temple? | Between 07:00 and about 09:30, when low sun shows the depth of the carving and there are fewer visitors.
Is the Red Temple old? | No, the carved red hall is a modern building in an old style, and work on parts of the site has continued in recent years.
What is near the Red Temple? | Hin Ta and Hin Yai about 1–2 km north, the Guan Yu Shrine about 1 km south, Hua Thanon fish market and Wat Khunaram about 5 km west.
